# Reference fixtures

All files are self-authored for Master Of Notes tests (Law 19): no third-party music.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `simple.json` | `mon-melody` v1, 5 notes, lyrics, one microtonal pitch (65.5). |
| `overlaps.json` | Chord at 0 ms (keep top), legato overlap going down (1500 ms), higher note inside a lower one (2100 ms), unsorted input. |
| `two-tracks.mid` | SMF type 1, 480 tpb, 120 BPM: tempo track, "Piano" (6 chord notes, ch 2), "Vocal" (4 notes). |
| `test-song.json` | Copy of the T-003-05 test song (`apps/desktop/e2e/tools/test-song.mon-melody.json`, self-authored): legato, repeated notes, a 150 ms note, a rest, a fifth leap. Frozen here for the scoring regression (amateur curve, vibrato targets). |
| `tempo-change.mid` | SMF type 1, 480 tpb: 120 BPM, then 60 BPM at tick 1920 (2000 ms); the note at tick 1680 crosses the change. |
| `ultrastar-simple.txt` | UltraStar, UTF-8 with BOM, BPM 300 (50 ms/beat), GAP 1000: normal and golden (`*`) notes, a `~` continuation, `F`/`R`/`G` lines (left out), a negative pitch, a note after `E` (ignored). |
| `ultrastar-cp1252-relative.txt` | UltraStar in Windows-1252 (accented syllables), `#BPM:250,0` (decimal comma), `#RELATIVE:yes` with two-number line breaks. |
| `ultrastar-duet.txt` | UltraStar duet: `P1` and `P2` at the same beats, then a `P3` (both) note; only P1 + P3 are imported. |

MIDI files were generated by a 40-line Python script writing raw SMF chunks
(no notation software); the UltraStar files were written by hand (melodies and
syllables of our own). Expected note times are asserted in
`crates/scoring-engine/tests/reference.rs`. Repo line endings are LF
(`.gitattributes`), so CRLF is tested with an inline string.
